title: Migrate legacy project_refs to surrogate IDs and introduce row-level compaction
creator: Morgan Ruiz
description:
Background: The control plane has two legacy join patterns around project_refs: (1) project_refs is a variable-width text FK stored in several hot tables, and (2) application-level code performs repeated lookups on project_keys which causes repeated index scans and inflated bloat. These legacy references are a major contributor to wide row widths, inefficient joins, and slowed index performance for tenant-heavy workloads.

Goal: Replace textual project reference keys with compact surrogate integers (project_id bigint) and add an opportunistic row-level compaction path that re-writes hot rows to remove deleted/legacy columns. The migration must be online with zero write downtime, support rollbacks, and reduce P95 read latency for the control-plane hot-read endpoints by at least 20% in production workloads.

Success criteria: 
- Primary: P95 query latency for control_plane.project_reads decreases >=20% within 2 weeks of rollout.
- Secondary: Estimated table bloat on hot tables (projects_metadata, project_events) decreases by >=30% measured via bloat_estimate metric.
- Migration completes without more than 5 minutes of sustained replica lag spikes during any step.

High-level approach: 
1) Add surrogate id column to canonical projects table (projects.surrogate_id bigint generated null initially).
2) Backfill surrogate ids in a consistent, idempotent background job (shadow writer) that writes to both legacy textual FK columns and the new surrogate_id. Backfill uses batched UPDATEs ordered by created_at to keep WAL spike bounded.
3) Introduce a small mapping table project_key_map(project_key text primary key, surrogate_id bigint unique) to support lookups for in-flight reads during the transition. 
4) Switch read paths in control-plane read service to prefer surrogate_id joins when available, falling back to project_key map otherwise. This is a read-only toggle first (feature-flagged).
5) Gradually migrate write paths to perform dual writes (legacy text field + surrogate_id) via SDK and background adapter layer.
6) After verification and monitoring, remove legacy text FKs and indexes and run a row-level compaction rewrite using pg_repack or an application-driven rewrite to reclaim space.
7) Final verification, index rebuilds optimized for new join shape, and prune mapping table compatibility layer.

Rollback plan: If issues detected (inc. >10% error rate or replica lag > 5m), flip feature flag to force reads back to text lookup only and pause background backfill. Mapping table and surrogate_id writes are additive—dropping them is not required for rollback.

Risks and mitigations: 
- WAL surge during backfill: mitigate by small batch sizes, rate limiter, and scheduling low-priority windows.
- Race on concurrent writes: use idempotent upsert patterns into project_key_map and strict ordering in dual-write adapters.
- Long-running transactions during compaction: use out-of-band rewrite (pg_repack) to avoid locks.

Observability & validation: Dashboards/metrics to monitor during migration: 
- control_plane.query_latency_95 (tag: endpoint=project_reads)
- pg.replica_lag_seconds
- db.index_scan_pct
- db.bloat_estimate_percent (hot tables)
- migration.project_key_map_mismatch_count

Validation queries (examples to run after each phase):
- "SELECT count(*) FROM projects WHERE surrogate_id IS NULL;"
- "SELECT count(*) FROM project_key_map WHERE not exists (SELECT 1 FROM projects p WHERE p.surrogate_id = project_key_map.surrogate_id);"
- "EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT p.* FROM projects p JOIN project_events e ON p.surrogate_id = e.project_id LIMIT 1;"

Links: 
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/CP-DB-Migrate-ProjectRefs (migration spec and risk register)
- Runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/cp-projectrefs-migration 
- GH PR template for dual-write adapters: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/xxxxx

Operational notes: 
- Coordinate with SRE for low-traffic windows (UTC 0200-0500) for heavy backfills.
- Reserve a small burst of Dedicated capacity for the 72-hour warm-up window to prevent queueing on serving APIs.

Estimated effort: 8 points (backfill job + read switch + dual-write adapters + compaction + monitoring + rollback testing).
migration_sql_examples: -- add column without locking: ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN surrogate_id bigint;
-- create mapping table: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS project_key_map (project_key text PRIMARY KEY, surrogate_id bigint UNIQUE);
-- idempotent upsert into mapping table: INSERT INTO project_key_map(project_key, surrogate_id) VALUES ('abc', 123) ON CONFLICT (project_key) DO UPDATE SET surrogate_id = EXCLUDED.surrogate_id;
-- compaction via pg_repack (example): pg_repack --table projects --dbname control_plane
updates: 2025-01-10 - Ticket created by Morgan Ruiz: initial spec and success criteria added; assigned to Priya Shah.
2025-01-15 - Design review: agreed to use a mapping table rather than modifying all FK constraints at once. Action: SRE coordination for backfill windows.
2025-01-20 - Engineering sync: dual-write adapter prototype submitted; small benchmark shows 2% p95 overhead on writes when dual-writing (acceptable).
2025-01-24 - QA: smoke tests for idempotent upsert passed on staging; found one edge case with deleted projects being re-created — added guard to upsert to ignore tombstones.
2025-01-28 - Deployment: feature-flagged read switch deployed to 10% of control-plane read capacity; no visible latency regression; monitoring dashboard updated.
2025-02-02 - Backfill started (low-priority batches). First 48h completed: 22% of rows backfilled, replica lag within thresholds; continuing with adjusted batch size to smooth WAL spikes.
notes_for_code_reviews: Ensure all dual-write paths use the same transaction boundary semantics as existing writes to avoid partial application.
Add detailed metrics for per-batch backfill progress and rollback counters.
Include integration tests that assert read-paths return identical results when both keys present.
Add feature-flag gating and a clear kill-switch for read switch.
Document expected index scans before and after to help reviewers evaluate index changes.
